property_summary: If a transaction has msg.value == 10 ether, then after the transaction, the contract balance should be zero only when block.number % 15 == 0.
After a successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether, if block.timestamp equals the stored pastBlockTime, the call must revert.
After a successful fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether, the timestamp stored in pastBlockTime is strictly greater than the previous pastBlockTime.
After a fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether that does not trigger a payout, the contract balance increases by exactly 10 ether.
If a fallback call with msg.value == 10 ether succeeds, then block.timestamp > pastBlockTime (the previous stored timestamp).
The contract's balance should never increase after a fallback call that does not revert.
After any fallback call that reverts or does not revert, the pastBlockTime state variable should only increase.
After any fallback call that does not revert, the contract's balance should always be zero.
After any call to fallback with msg.value equal to 10 ether, if the block number is a multiple of 15, the contract balance becomes 0.
If at least 10 ether is sent to the contract, the contract can never have a positive balance after a fallback call at a block number that is a multiple of 15.
After any fallback call that does not revert, the contract's balance must be at most the sum of all msg.value sent - 10 ether for each call that executed the original require.
After every successful fallback call with msg.value >= 10 ether, the contract balance is either 0 or unchanged from before the call.
If exactly 10 ether is sent and block.number % 15 == 0, the contract balance becomes 0.
After any call to fallback that succeeds, pastBlockTime is updated to the current block.timestamp.
After any successful fallback call that does not trigger a transfer (i.e., when block.number % 15 != 0), pastBlockTime must equal block.timestamp at the time of that call.
When fallback is called with a new block timestamp, pastBlockTime is always set to the timestamp of that block.
After a successful fallback call that transfers ether (block.number % 15 == 0), the caller must receive at least 10 ether.
After any successful fallback call, pastBlockTime must equal block.timestamp at the time of that call, regardless of whether the transfer occurred.
